libtmux for Erlang

Hex.pm · Documentation · API reference · Examples

Drive tmux from Erlang: create [sessions][tmux-session], [windows][tmux-window] and [panes][tmux-pane], capture the [object graph][tmux-snapshot] as immutable data, filter it, ask tmux again. [Install](#install) · [Create, capture and query](#create-capture-and-query) · [Find and filter](#find-and-filter) · [Plan and optimise](#plan-and-optimise-a-query) · [Batch commands](#run-commands-together) · [Own a server](#own-a-server-and-wait-for-work) · [Packages](#packages) · [Core package](apps/libtmux_erlang/README.md) · [Support](#support-and-status) · [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md) ## Install It needs: - Erlang/OTP 29 and Rebar3. - tmux 3.3a or newer, on Linux (including WSL). - `make` and a C11 compiler, to build the bundled helper. Add the core from [Hex](https://hex.pm/packages/libtmux_erlang) to your `rebar.config`: ```erlang {deps, [{libtmux_erlang, "0.0.1"}]}. ``` The API is still developing. Pin an exact version and commit `rebar.lock`. More: [installation guide](docs/installation.md). ## Create, capture and query ### [`tmux_server:with_owned/2`][api-with-owned]: create a private tmux graph The example below uses four modules: - [`tmux_server`][tmux-server]: owns the connection and the server's lifetime. - [`tmux_snapshot`][tmux-snapshot]: holds captured rows. - [`tmux_select`][tmux-select]: filters those rows locally. - [`tmux_query`][tmux-query]: asks tmux again when fetched. From a checkout of this repository, compile it: ```console $ mise exec -- rebar3 compile ``` Run it on a private tmux server: ```console $ mise exec -- escript tools/run_examples.escript readme ``` It starts an empty daemon on its own socket, then stops that daemon and its clients. Your existing sessions are untouched. To reuse the program, save it as `readme_demo.erl`. ```erlang -module(readme_demo). -moduledoc "Create a workspace, query its graph and preserve captured values.". -export([run/1]). -import_record(tmux_model, [pane]). -spec run(binary()) -> map(). run(Executable) -> Options = #{executable => Executable}, {ok, Result} = tmux_server:with_owned(Options, fun(Server) -> {ok, Session} = tmux_session:create(Server, #{name => <<"workspace">>, window_name => <<"editor">>, width => 120, height => 30, launch => #{argv => [<<"/bin/cat">>]}}), {ok, Worker} = tmux_window:create(Session, #{name => <<"workers">>, launch => #{argv => [<<"/bin/cat">>]}}), {ok, Right} = tmux_pane:split(Worker, #{direction => horizontal, launch => #{argv => [<<"/bin/cat">>]}}), {ok, _} = tmux_window:select_layout(Worker, even_horizontal), {ok, _} = tmux_pane:resize(Right, #{width => 40}), {ok, Snapshot} = tmux_server:snapshot(Server), Windows = tmux_select:windows(Snapshot), Workers = #{name => <<"workers">>, panes => #{count => 2, every => #{current_command => <<"cat">>}}}, {ok, Captured} = tmux_select:one(Workers, Windows), {ok, Children} = tmux_snapshot:related(panes, Captured, Snapshot), Ids = [Id || #pane{id = Id} <:- Children], 2 = length(Ids), Criteria = #{width => #{gte => 20}, window => #{is => #{name => <<"workers">>}}}, Query = tmux_query:where(Criteria, tmux_query:panes(Server)), {ok, Fetched} = tmux_query:fetch(Query), 2 = tmux_select:size(Fetched), {ok, _} = tmux_window:rename(Worker, <<"finished">>), <<"workers">> = tmux_model:get(name, Captured), {ok, Fresh} = tmux_query:fetch(tmux_query:where( #{name => <<"finished">>}, tmux_query:windows(Server))), {ok, Renamed} = tmux_select:one(Fresh), <<"finished">> = tmux_model:get(name, Renamed), 1 = length(tmux_snapshot:sessions(Snapshot)), 2 = length(tmux_snapshot:windows(Snapshot)), 3 = length(tmux_snapshot:panes(Snapshot)), #{sessions => 1, windows => 2, panes => 3, matched_panes => 2, captured_name => <<"workers">>, immutable => true} end), Result. ``` It returns: ```json { "sessions": 1, "windows": 2, "panes": 3, "matched_panes": 2, "captured_name": "workers", "immutable": true } ``` - Captured rows keep their values after the rename. Actions and `fetch` do I/O. - `with_owned/2` returns after verified cleanup. If cleanup fails, the error keeps the callback's outcome and the ownership token. More: [Daemon ownership](docs/ownership.md). ### [`tmux_pane:send_text/2`][api-send-text] and [`tmux_pane:capture/2`][api-capture]: type into a pane and read it back [`tmux_pane:send_keys/2`][api-send-keys] sends named keys such as Enter. A send returns before the program reads it, so the shell signals a tmux channel and the program awaits that signal before it captures: ```console $ mise exec -- escript tools/run_examples.escript typing ``` ```erlang -module(typing_demo). -moduledoc "Type a command into a shell pane, wait for it, read the screen.". -export([run/1]). -spec run(binary()) -> map(). run(Executable) -> {ok, Result} = tmux_server:with_owned(#{executable => Executable}, fun(Server) -> Shell = #{argv => [<<"/bin/sh">>]}, {ok, _} = tmux_session:create(Server, #{name => <<"typing">>, width => 120, height => 30, launch => Shell}), {ok, Snapshot} = tmux_server:snapshot(Server), [Pane] = tmux_snapshot:panes(Snapshot), % The shell signals a tmux channel once it has printed. {ok, Wait} = tmux_command:wait_for(<<"typed">>, wait), {ok, Operation} = tmux_operation:start(Server, Wait, #{}), Signal = <<"'", Executable/binary, "' wait-for -S typed">>, Line = <<"echo hello; ", Signal/binary>>, {ok, _} = tmux_pane:send_text(Pane, Line), {ok, _} = tmux_pane:send_keys(Pane, [enter]), {ok, _} = tmux_operation:await(Operation, 2000), {ok, Screen} = tmux_pane:capture(Pane, #{}), Rows = binary:split(Screen, <<"\n">>, [global]), true = lists:member(<<"hello">>, Rows), #{typed => <<"echo hello">>, screen_row => <<"hello">>} end), Result. ``` It returns: ```json { "typed": "echo hello", "screen_row": "hello" } ``` - [`tmux_pane:kill/1`][api-kill-pane], [`tmux_window:kill/1`][api-kill-window] and [`tmux_session:kill/1`][api-kill-session] remove one target. - [`tmux_option:set/3`][api-option-set] and [`tmux_option:get/3`][api-option-get] write and read options; [`tmux_hook:set/3`][api-hook-set] and [`tmux_hook:get/3`][api-hook-get] do the same for hooks. More: [Wait for a terminal job, then capture its output](docs/jobs.md). ## Find and filter ### [`tmux_snapshot:related/3`][api-related]: follow shared windows A window can be linked more than once in a session, and into several sessions. Physical windows and panes stay unique; each link keeps its session and index. More: [Linked windows and relationship queries](docs/graph.md). ### [`tmux_select:where/2`][api-where]: filter captured rows Filtering runs locally on captured rows and never calls tmux. [`tmux_filter`][tmux-filter] validates a filter and encodes it as portable JSON. This program needs no tmux server: ```console $ mise exec -- escript tools/run_examples.escript filter ``` ```erlang -module(filter_demo). -moduledoc "Validate portable JSON and filter captured rows without tmux I/O.". -export([run/0]). -spec run() -> map(). run() -> {ok, Editor} = tmux_model:pane(#{id => <<"%1">>, active => true, width => 120, current_command => <<"nvim">>}), {ok, Shell} = tmux_model:pane(#{id => <<"%2">>, active => false, width => 80, current_command => <<"bash">>}), Panes = tmux_select:from_list(pane, [Editor, Shell]), Criteria = #{active => true, 'or' => [ #{current_command => #{in => [<<"nvim">>, <<"vim">>]}}, #{width => #{gte => 160}} ]}, {ok, Filter} = tmux_filter:new(pane, Criteria), Encoded = iolist_to_binary(json:encode(tmux_filter:to_wire(Filter))), {ok, Document} = tmux_filter:decode_json(Encoded), {ok, RoundTrip} = tmux_filter:from_wire(pane, Document), {ok, Editor} = tmux_select:one(RoundTrip, Panes), [Editor] = tmux_select:to_list(tmux_select:where(Filter, Panes)), {error, #{code := duplicate_key}} = tmux_filter:decode_json( <<"{\"version\":1,\"version\":2}">>), Invalid = #{active => #{contains => <<"yes">>}}, try tmux_select:where(Invalid, Panes) of _ -> error(expected_validation_error) catch error:{bad_filter, #{code := unsupported_operator} = Detail}:Stack -> [active, contains] = maps:get(path, Detail), Reason = {bad_filter, Detail}, Message = erl_error:format_exception(error, Reason, Stack), Text = unicode:characters_to_binary(Message), {_, _} = binary:match(Text, <<"Allowed:">>) end, #{matched_ids => [tmux_model:get(id, Editor)], wire_round_trip => true, duplicate_keys_rejected => true}. ``` It returns: ```json { "matched_ids": ["%1"], "wire_round_trip": true, "duplicate_keys_rejected": true } ``` - Criteria are maps or Boolean functions, with quantifiers and portable JSON. - An unknown field or operator fails before any row is read. More: [Local filters and source queries](docs/querying.md) · [Fields and operators](docs/fields.md). ### [`tmux_query:fetch/1`][api-fetch]: read tmux again A query asks tmux when you fetch it and returns a new immutable selection. Rows you already hold keep their values. More: [Local filters and source queries](docs/querying.md). ## Plan and optimise a query ### [`tmux_query:explain/1`][api-explain]: see what tmux runs `explain/1` describes a query without calling tmux. This program explains one query twice, then fetches it and checks that the rows agree: ```console $ mise exec -- escript tools/run_examples.escript plan ``` ```erlang -module(plan_demo). -moduledoc "Explain a query, let tmux exclude candidates, then fetch it.". -export([run/1]). -spec run(binary()) -> map(). run(Executable) -> {ok, Result} = tmux_server:with_owned(#{executable => Executable}, fun(Server) -> Cat = #{launch => #{argv => [<<"/bin/cat">>]}}, Wide = Cat#{name => <<"plan">>, width => 120, height => 30}, {ok, Session} = tmux_session:create(Server, Wide), {ok, Window} = tmux_window:create(Session, Cat), {ok, _} = tmux_pane:split(Window, Cat#{direction => horizontal}), Criteria = #{width => #{lt => 100}, current_command => <<"cat">>}, Query = tmux_query:where(Criteria, tmux_query:panes(Server)), Pushed = tmux_query:pushdown(true, Query), % explain/1 does no I/O: it only describes what fetch would run. #{candidate := #{format := Local}} = tmux_query:explain(Query), #{candidate := #{format := Native, local_only := Kept}} = tmux_query:explain(Pushed), {ok, Everything} = tmux_query:fetch(Query), {ok, Narrowed} = tmux_query:fetch(Pushed), {ok, Isolated} = tmux_query:fetch(Pushed, #{hydration => isolated}), Ids = ids(Narrowed), 2 = length(Ids), Ids = ids(Everything), Ids = ids(Isolated), #{local_candidate => Local, native_candidate => Native, kept_local => [maps:get(field, Reason) || Reason <- Kept], matched_panes => length(Ids), same_rows => true} end), Result. ids(Selection) -> [tmux_model:get(id, Pane) || Pane <- tmux_select:to_list(Selection)]. ``` It returns: ```json { "local_candidate": "1", "native_candidate": "#{e|<|:#{pane_width},100}", "kept_local": ["tmux.pane.currentCommand"], "matched_panes": 2, "same_rows": true } ``` - `local_candidate`: without pushdown, tmux drops nothing. - `native_candidate`: the tmux format that drops rows before capture. - `kept_local`: fields tmux cannot filter stay in Erlang. More: [Source plans](docs/querying.md#source-plans). ### [`tmux_query:pushdown/2`][api-pushdown]: let tmux drop rows first Pushdown is off by default. Turn it on to add a candidate scan that excludes rows before capture. The full filter still runs locally, so a candidate can admit extra rows but never hides a match. The program above also fetches with `hydration => isolated`, which reads one field per row when a single scan would pass the output limit. Captures span several commands and are not atomic. More: [Source plans](docs/querying.md#source-plans). ## Run commands together ### [`tmux_command:sequence/1`][api-sequence]: several commands, one call Build commands without I/O, join them and run them once. A sequence is not atomic: a failing member can leave the commands before it applied. ```console $ mise exec -- escript tools/run_examples.escript batch ``` ```erlang -module(batch_demo). -moduledoc "Run several commands in one tmux client and read an option batch.". -export([run/1]). -spec run(binary()) -> map(). run(Executable) -> {ok, Result} = tmux_server:with_owned(#{executable => Executable}, fun(Server) -> Cat = #{launch => #{argv => [<<"/bin/cat">>]}}, {ok, Session} = tmux_session:create(Server, Cat#{name => <<"batch">>}), {ok, Window} = tmux_window:create(Session, Cat), Id = tmux_model:get(id, Session), {ok, Rename} = tmux_session:rename_command(Session, <<"batched">>), {ok, Stage} = tmux_command:raw(<<"set-option">>, [<<"-t">>, Id, <<"@stage">>, <<"built">>]), {ok, Owner} = tmux_command:raw(<<"set-option">>, [<<"-t">>, Id, <<"@owner">>, <<"batch-demo">>]), % Three commands, one native sequence. A failure can leave a prefix. {ok, Sequence} = tmux_command:sequence([Rename, Stage, Owner]), {ok, #{exit_status := 0}} = tmux_server:command(Server, Sequence, #{}), {ok, Renamed} = tmux_session:get(Server, Id), {ok, [<<"built">>, none]} = tmux_option:get_many([Session, Window], <<"@stage">>, #{}), #{commands => 3, session_name => tmux_model:get(name, Renamed), stage => <<"built">>, window_stage => none} end), Result. ``` It returns: ```json { "commands": 3, "session_name": "batched", "stage": "built", "window_stage": "none" } ``` - [`tmux_option:get_many/3`][api-get-many] reads one option from up to seven rows in one batch. More: [Build command values](docs/commands.md) · [Scoped options](docs/options.md). ## Own a server and wait for work ### [`tmux_server:with_server/2`][api-with-server]: borrow an existing server Closing the handle leaves the borrowed server and its sessions alone. [`tmux_server:with_owned/2`][api-with-owned] starts a private one instead. More: [Daemon ownership](docs/ownership.md) · [Control attachments](docs/control.md). ### [`tmux_control:attach/3`][api-attach]: hold a control attachment Attach to a session over a persistent connection, check its identity on that connection, then close it and confirm cleanup. Commands still run through one-shot clients; control command submission and output streams are not built. ```console $ mise exec -- escript tools/run_examples.escript control ``` ```erlang -module(control_demo). -moduledoc "Attach explicitly, inspect captured values and prove detachment.". -export([run/2]). -spec run(binary(), binary()) -> map(). run(Socket, Executable) -> {ok, Server} = tmux_server:open( #{socket_path => Socket, executable => Executable}), tmux_scope:run_or_error(fun() -> {ok, Session} = tmux_session:create(Server, #{name => <<"control-demo">>, width => 120, height => 30, launch => #{argv => [<<"/bin/cat">>]}}), tmux_scope:run_or_error(fun() -> Id = tmux_model:get(id, Session), 0 = tmux_model:get(attached_count, Session), {ok, Control} = tmux_control:attach(Server, Session, #{}), tmux_scope:run_or_error(fun() -> {ok, #{phase := open, identity := same_connection}} = tmux_control:status(Control), {ok, Attached} = tmux_session:get(Server, Id), 1 = tmux_model:get(attached_count, Attached), {ok, Graph} = tmux_server:snapshot(Server), [Window] = tmux_snapshot:windows(Graph), 120 = tmux_model:get(width, Window), 30 = tmux_model:get(height, Window), ok = tmux_control:close(Control), {ok, #{phase := closed, cleanup := complete}} = tmux_control:status(Control), {ok, Detached} = tmux_session:get(Server, Id), 0 = tmux_model:get(attached_count, Detached), 0 = tmux_model:get(attached_count, Session), #{identity => same_connection, attached_count => 1, detached_count => 0, window_size => [120, 30], cleanup => complete, session_preserved => true} end, fun() -> ok = tmux_control:close(Control) end) end, fun() -> {ok, _} = tmux_session:kill(Session), ok end) end, fun() -> ok = tmux_server:close(Server) end). ``` It returns: ```json { "identity": "same_connection", "attached_count": 1, "detached_count": 0, "window_size": [120, 30], "cleanup": "complete", "session_preserved": true } ``` More: [Control attachments](docs/control.md). ### [`tmux_pane:wait_exit/2`][api-wait-exit]: wait for a job to exit Wait for a pane's process and read how it ended: `{status, Code}` for an exit status, `{signal, Signal}` for a death by signal. The pane keeps its dead state through `remain-on-exit`. More: [Run a job and capture its result](docs/jobs.md). ### [`tmux_operation:await/2`][api-await]: wait for submitted work Submit an operation without blocking, then await it, cancel it or hand it to another process. Capture a job's exit status and output bytes. More: [Run a job and capture its result](docs/jobs.md) · [Build command values](docs/commands.md). ## More examples - [Scoped options](docs/options.md): local, inherited and sparse-array options. - [Buffers and paste](docs/buffers.md): binary data and terminal delivery. - [Rearrange panes](docs/panes.md): move a running job to its own window and back. - [Apply configuration and await a signal](docs/configuration.md): load settings from stdin. - [Pipe terminal output](docs/pipe.md): save a job's bytes to a log. - [Hooks and completion](docs/hooks.md): register a split hook and remove it. - [Key tables](docs/keys.md): add application bindings and remove them. - [Native commands](docs/commands-reference.md): parser metadata and feature minimums for each tmux command. - [API browser and source docs](docs/api.md): build the reference pages with specs, types and source links. ## Packages | Package | What it is | Hex | | --- | --- | --- | | [`libtmux_erlang`](apps/libtmux_erlang/README.md) | The core OTP application: servers, sessions, windows, panes, snapshots and queries. | [![libtmux_erlang](https://img.shields.io/hexpm/v/libtmux_erlang?label=libtmux_erlang)](https://hex.pm/packages/libtmux_erlang) | ### [`libtmux_erlang`](https://github.com/libtmux/libtmux-erlang/tree/master/apps/libtmux_erlang): the core application Servers, sessions, windows, panes, snapshots and queries, with a bundled C helper for bounded tmux I/O. [![libtmux_erlang](https://img.shields.io/hexpm/v/libtmux_erlang?label=libtmux_erlang)](https://hex.pm/packages/libtmux_erlang) [API reference](https://libtmux.org/en/erlang/latest/reference/) · [Documentation](https://libtmux.org/en/erlang/) · [Hex.pm](https://hex.pm/packages/libtmux_erlang) · [Changelog](apps/libtmux_erlang/CHANGELOG.md) More: [package README](apps/libtmux_erlang/README.md) inspects an existing socket. ## Support and status - **Status:** early. Any release may change the API. - **Platform:** Linux, including WSL. macOS and native Windows are not advertised. - **tmux:** 3.3a or newer. A release newer than the tested ones returns `unsupported_option_catalogue` for built-in options and hooks. - **Erlang/OTP:** 29 only. The application refuses to start on another release. Rows are native records, which OTP 29 marks experimental. - **Dependencies:** OTP only. The helper is an external program, not a NIF. - **Operations:** an await timeout abandons the wait; it does not cancel the operation. Cancelling after dispatch can leave the tmux outcome unknown. # Install the core application

The core OTP application is
[`libtmux_erlang`](https://hex.pm/packages/libtmux_erlang) on Hex.

The [README](../README.md#install) has the dependency declaration. Pin an exact
version while the API develops, and commit `rebar.lock` to keep the resolved
package checksum.

Add `libtmux_erlang` to your application's `applications` list in its
`.app.src`. To try it interactively, compile and start the Rebar3 shell:

```console
$ rebar3 compile
```

```console
$ rebar3 shell
```

## Install a source checkout

The repository is an umbrella. Use `git_subdir` to select
`apps/libtmux_erlang`:

<!-- erlang-term -->

```erlang
{deps, [
    {libtmux_erlang, {git_subdir,
        "https://github.com/libtmux/libtmux-erlang.git",
        {branch, "master"}, "apps/libtmux_erlang"}}
]}.
```

- Rebar3 records the branch's resolved commit in `rebar.lock`.
- To pin a reviewed commit, use `{ref, Commit}` instead of
  `{branch, "master"}`.

## Inspect an existing server

`open/1` borrows an existing daemon. It starts no tmux and creates no session.
The library needs the socket's absolute path. From a shell attached to the
server you want to inspect, get it:

```console
$ export LIBTMUX_SOCKET="$(tmux display-message -p '#{socket_path}')"
```

Save this module as `src/inspect_demo.erl` in the consumer application:

<!-- example: examples/inspect_demo.erl -->

```erlang
-module(inspect_demo).
-moduledoc "Inspect an existing tmux socket without changing its sessions.".
-export([run/2]).

-spec run(binary(), binary()) -> map().
run(Socket, Executable) ->
    {ok, _} = application:ensure_all_started(libtmux_erlang),
    Endpoint = #{socket_path => Socket, executable => Executable},
    {ok, Result} = tmux_server:with_server(Endpoint, fun(Server) ->
        {ok, Snapshot} = tmux_server:snapshot(Server),
        #{sessions => length(tmux_snapshot:sessions(Snapshot)),
          windows => length(tmux_snapshot:windows(Snapshot)),
          panes => length(tmux_snapshot:panes(Snapshot))}
    end),
    Result.
```

Run it through the consumer's Rebar shell. The tmux executable comes from
`PATH`. The socket must be the absolute path above:

```console
$ rebar3 shell \
    --eval '
        Socket = list_to_binary(os:getenv("LIBTMUX_SOCKET")),
        Tmux = list_to_binary(os:find_executable("tmux")),
        io:format("~p~n", [inspect_demo:run(Socket, Tmux)]),
        halt().'
```

- The returned map counts physical objects in one captured view.
- Closing the library handle leaves the borrowed daemon and its sessions.
- The [README program](../README.md#create-capture-and-query) starts its own
  private server. It adds creation, native record patterns, graph traversal
  and a fresh query.
- To build a native record yourself, load `tmux_model` first. Its constructors
  load normally and validate observations.
- Do not distribute record headers or serialize record internals as a wire
  format.
