The program uses a unique buffer name and deletes the buffer in cleanup.

## Choose a name or the newest buffer

- `tmux_buffer:load/3` takes a binary name or `automatic`, which lets tmux pick
  one.
- `show/2`, `delete/2` and `paste/3` take an observed binary name or `latest`.
- `list/1` returns metadata maps, newest first, with name, size in bytes and
  Unix creation time. It loads no payloads.
- Renaming keeps the order. Loading replacement data inserts a new buffer.
- Names are NUL-free bytes. tmux 3.7 and newer clean names themselves, which
  can reject controls and escape backslashes. Later calls need the stored name
  from `list/1`.
- The list codec keeps embedded delimiters, newlines and invalid UTF-8 where a
  release allows those names. It never treats a newline in a name as a row
  boundary.

## Know the version differences

- An empty load is a native no-op. It creates no buffer and does not truncate
  an existing one. Delete a buffer to remove it.
- Renaming onto an occupied name is refused on tmux 3.3 and 3.3a. From 3.4 it
  replaces. Identical rename inputs fail before dispatch, because some old
  versions handle them unsafely.
- On 3.3 and 3.3a, a native delete or rename of a missing name falls back to
  the newest buffer. These APIs first check that the name exists, with no
  output allowance, and return `buffer_not_found` if not. The check keeps no
  payload and ignores list bounds.
- That check is not atomic. A concurrent removal after it can still trigger the
  native fallback. Serialize outside changes or use tmux 3.4 or newer.
- Buffer names are neither stable identities nor transactional.

## Paste bytes into a registered pane

- `tmux_buffer:paste/3` takes a registered pane, a buffer name or `latest`, and
  an options map.
- Defaults preserve bytes: LF separators, no sanitizing, no bracketing, no
  deletion.
- `separator` replaces each LF with a NUL-free byte string. It is passed
  literally, with no format expansion.
- `sanitize => true` needs tmux 3.7 or newer. Older releases return
  `unsupported_capability` before dispatch. The raw path uses `-S` on newer
  releases.
- `bracketed => true` adds markers only when the target enabled bracketed
  paste.
- `delete => true` removes the buffer after the native paste, including when
  native input-off handling discards the input.
- A completed paste is a tmux command result. It does not prove a child consumed
  the input. See the [job guide](jobs.md) for completion signals and
  ownership.

## Bound reads and keep errors

- Load input shares the endpoint's 256 KiB command admission budget with argv.
- `show/3` takes `max_bytes` from 0 through 1 MiB and `deadline_ms` from 1
  through 600000. Defaults are 1 MiB and 2500 ms.
- Overflow returns `output_limit` with partial command evidence. A truncated
  buffer is never returned as success.
- Lists are bounded to 4096 rows and 1 MiB of encoded output.
- Missing buffers, gone panes and closed endpoints stay distinct errors.
- A timeout does not undo a completed load or paste. Mutations are not retried.
- `tmux_buffer:capabilities/1` describes source-defined behavior without I/O.
  The [support page](compatibility.md) separates that metadata from what is
  tested.

## Select the table explicitly

| Scope argument | Table |
| --- | --- |
| Registered session record | Local session options |
| Registered physical window record | Local window options, shared by its memberships |
| Registered pane record | Local pane options |
| `{server, Server}` | Server-wide options |
| `{session_defaults, Server}` | Global session defaults |
| `{window_defaults, Server}` | Global window defaults |

- A physical window has no universal parent session. Session options need a
  session record; a pane passed to one fails instead of picking a session.
- Built-in names can override tmux's native scope flags. The wrapper checks
  their source metadata before dispatch to prevent that.
- `get/3` reads local values only with `#{}`.
- `#{inherit => true}` follows the table's parents: session defaults, or window
  defaults for a pane. User options follow the same ancestry. Server options
  have no parent. A session table never passes values to a window table.

## Read many rows at once

- `tmux_option:get_many/3` reads one scalar key from one to seven local rows on
  one registered endpoint. Results keep input order, with `none` for absent
  values.
- The program reads the session's ownership and the window's own local table
  together.
- Arrays, indexed entries, command options, global tables and names outside the
  batch grammar use `get/3`.
- A batch is one native command sequence plus the normal identity-preflight
  client, with native ID observations around each row's read.
- Output is capped at 1 MiB of stdout and 64 KiB of stderr, with a 2500 ms
  deadline. A command or decoding failure rejects the whole batch.
- These are interval observations. A queued reference can outlive a removed
  window, and the target checks are not atomic. See
  [ADR 0003](adr-0003-scoped-option-batches.md).

## Preserve absence and bytes

- `none` means the selected local option or array entry is absent.
  `{ok, <<>>}` means a known empty value.
- A whole array returns `{ok, Entries}` with numeric indexes as keys. An empty
  local array returns `{ok, #{}}`.
- Set an entry with `{Name, Index}`. There is no whole-array assignment.
- `unset/2` removes an entry or local option. Removing a local option restores
  inheritance. Unsetting a global built-in resets its tmux default.
- Non-numeric array keys are outside this API. An observed array with such keys
  fails decoding instead of dropping entries.
- Values are NUL-free binaries and may hold any other byte.
- Names are literal. `#{...}` in a user-option name does not expand. Prefixes,
  aliases and bracket syntax are rejected.
- A scalar value goes out without `-F`, but tmux may later interpret a stored
  format or command option. Use this API only with trusted names and values.
- `append` uses tmux's `-a` for the option's type. `only_if_unset` uses `-o`
  and reports an already-set option as an error.
- An empty flag value keeps tmux's toggle behavior. Use `<<"on">>` or
  `<<"off">>` when the state must be predictable.
- A mutation is not retried after a timeout or unknown outcome.

## Discover version support

- The [generated catalogue](options-reference.md) lists canonical names, scopes,
  parser types, arrays and hooks from pinned release commits.
- `tmux_option:describe/2` and `catalogue/1` read it without I/O.
- Built-ins have exact catalogues for every release from 3.3a through 3.8,
  including patch releases. A tracking build or unknown version returns
  `unsupported_option_catalogue`. An unavailable built-in returns
  `unsupported_tmux_option`. User options need no catalogue.
- This API rejects hooks, including names found in the catalogue. Use
  `tmux_hook:get/3` and `tmux_hook:set/3`; the [hook guide](hooks.md) covers
  scope, execution and cleanup.
- Raw commands remain available for deliberate newer-version work.
- A missing target is an operational error, never a missing option.

# Register a hook and await its effect

Register a split hook, submit a wait without blocking the caller, then split a
pane. The hook writes a session option and signals a unique channel.

- The program checks the option, removes the local hook and verifies cleanup.
- It cancels and awaits its operation in cleanup, even when registration or
  the split fails.
- The runner supplies the daemon.

```console
$ mise exec -- rebar3 compile
```

Run the complete program:

```console
$ mise exec -- escript tools/run_examples.escript hooks
```

```erlang
-module(hook_demo).
-moduledoc "Acknowledge a registered split hook before reading its effect.".
-export([run/2]).

-spec run(binary(), binary()) -> map().
run(Socket, Executable) ->
    {ok, Server} = tmux_server:open(
        #{socket_path => Socket, executable => Executable}),
    tmux_scope:run_or_error(fun() ->
        Launch = #{launch => #{argv => [<<"/bin/cat">>]}},
        {ok, Session} = tmux_session:create(Server,
            Launch#{name => <<"hooks">>}),
        tmux_scope:run_or_error(fun() ->
            {ok, Snapshot} = tmux_server:snapshot(Server),
            [Pane] = tmux_snapshot:panes(Snapshot),
            Suffix = binary:encode_hex(crypto:strong_rand_bytes(8), lowercase),
            Channel = <<"hook-", Suffix/binary>>,
            {ok, Mark} = tmux_command:raw(<<"set-option">>,
                [<<"-t">>, tmux_model:get(id, Session),
                 <<"@last-event">>, <<"split complete">>]),
            {ok, Signal} = tmux_command:wait_for(Channel, signal),
            {ok, Wait} = tmux_command:wait_for(Channel, wait),
            {ok, Operation} = tmux_operation:start(Server, Wait, #{}),
            tmux_scope:run_or_error(fun() ->
                Name = <<"after-split-window">>,
                {ok, _} = tmux_hook:set(Session, {Name, 4}, [Mark, Signal]),
                {ok, _} = tmux_pane:split(Pane, Launch),
                {ok, #{cleanup := complete}} =
                    tmux_operation:await(Operation, 900),
                {ok, <<"split complete">>} =
                    tmux_option:get(Session, <<"@last-event">>, #{}),
                {ok, #{4 := _}} = tmux_hook:get(Session, Name, #{}),
                {ok, _} = tmux_hook:unset(Session, Name),
                none = tmux_hook:get(Session, Name, #{}),
                #{event => <<"split complete">>, hook_acknowledged => true,
                  local_hook_removed => true}
            end, fun() ->
                tmux_scope:run_or_error(fun() ->
                    {ok, _} = tmux_operation:cancel(Operation)
                end, fun() ->
                    case tmux_operation:await(Operation, 900) of
                        {ok, #{cleanup := complete}} -> ok;
                        {error, #{cleanup := complete}} -> ok
                    end
                end), ok
            end)
        end, fun() ->
            {ok, _} = tmux_session:kill(Session),
            ok
        end)
    end, fun() ->
        ok = tmux_server:close(Server)
    end).
```

## Choose the table

- `tmux_hook:set/3` needs a `{Name, Index}` key and validated `tmux_command`
  values. It replaces that indexed entry and keeps the others.
- `append/3` takes tmux's first vacant local index, which can come before
  existing sparse entries. Commands run in index order.
- A body is one command or a nonempty list. Rendering is bounded before
  dispatch.
- Local tables use registered session, physical window or pane rows. Global
  tables use `{session_defaults, Server}` or `{window_defaults, Server}`.
- The [source catalogue](options-reference.md) gives each built-in hook's scope
  and version.
- This API rejects prefixes, aliases, ordinary options and custom event or
  monitor interfaces.

## Read and remove

- `get/3` reads local values by default. `inherit => true` follows parent
  tables.
- An absent local array returns `none`. An empty array returns `{ok, #{}}` and
  masks inheritance.
- `clear/2` leaves that empty override. `unset/2` removes an entry, or restores
  inheritance for the whole array. Unsetting an entry can leave the local array
  empty. A global unset resets the native default.
- Read values are tmux's canonical command-list text, with its own quoting and
  escapes. They are not argument values or the original source. A read never
  runs them.

## Registration, context and completion

- Registration confirms that tmux stored the commands. They still interpret
  their values and formats when they run.
- Native parsing can fail. A failed first indexed write can already leave an
  empty local override.
- There is no rollback and no automatic retry of an uncertain mutation.
- `tmux_hook:run/2` requests native execution in an explicit context: a session
  for its current window and pane, a checked window link for one membership, or
  `{pane, Pane, Link}` for a pane and membership.
- A physical window alone cannot choose a context, so a link keeps the session
  and index when a window is linked more than once.
- Existence and membership checks come before dispatch. If the target vanishes
  afterward, tmux can still fall back to another context. These observations
  are not atomic.
- A command result does not acknowledge background work a hook launched. The
  program waits for its own signal after the option write.
- Clearing or unsetting a hook does not cancel effects tmux already queued.

See [window memberships](graph.md) and [scoped options](options.md) for the
graph and inheritance rules.

## Register a binding

- `tmux_key:bind/3` registers in the native prefix table.
- `tmux_key:bind/4` takes an explicit `table`, a Boolean `repeat` and a byte
  `note`.
- A body is one command or a flat nonempty list, within the limits of
  `tmux_command:to_config/1`: 256 commands and 32 KiB of rendered text.
- tmux parses the body before it replaces an existing binding. Replacement
  resets the old commands, repeat flag and note.
- Tables belong to the server. Creating one selects it for no client. Choose a
  session's default with the `key-table` option in [`tmux_option`](options.md).
  Native prefix, repeat and table-switching rules still apply.
- Registration quotes arguments for the stored command parser. A command can
  still expand formats when a client runs it: the program's `#{session_name}`
  expands then. See [configuration](configuration.md) before you store nested
  command strings or shell commands.
- An accepted registration does not prove future execution. When you need proof,
  arrange a completion signal as in the [hook example](hooks.md).

## Read listings and remove bindings

- `tmux_key:listing/1` and `listing/2` return native bytes unchanged. Options
  can restrict `table` and `key`.
- The layout follows the daemon release. It is a display view: keep the
  original command values to reinstall bindings.
- tmux 3.4 may escape dollar signs in this view.
- On tmux 3.7c, one matching entry can take the native status-message path and
  give empty stdout when no client is attached. Empty output does not prove a
  binding is absent. The program lists several bindings to avoid that path.
- tmux 3.3 has no custom listing format option. Newer-server options stay
  available through `tmux_command:raw/2`.
- `tmux_key:unbind/2` and `unbind/3` remove one binding. An absent key in an
  existing table is a native no-op. Removing the last custom binding can remove
  its table.
- A missing named table and an invalid key name stay errors.
- `tmux_key:clear_table/2` needs an explicit name and removes the whole table.
  It can affect attached clients. It does not restore default bindings or
  cancel commands a client already queued.
- Calls use the registered endpoint identity and keep backend diagnostics. They
  never start a missing server or retry an uncertain mutation.
- The [API browser](api.md) documents input bounds, results and errors.

## Render configuration

- `tmux_command:to_config/1` renders one validated command, or a nonempty flat
  list, as native configuration text. It does no I/O.
- A list holds at most 256 commands and shares the 32 KiB rendered limit,
  including native separators. Rendering a list gives no atomic execution or
  rollback.
- Quoting keeps literal bytes through the lexer: variables, semicolons,
  newline indentation and non-UTF-8 bytes. The result is ASCII text.
- That covers one lexer pass. Native commands that take command strings can
  parse those strings again, so render each inner command separately for its
  own boundary.
- Native commands still interpret their arguments and formats. The renderer
  does not quote shell code.

## Source a file or stdin

- `tmux_command:source_file/2` builds a command value without I/O. The source
  is `stdin` or one absolute POSIX byte path.
- Glob characters and backslashes in a path are quoted for tmux's glob parser.
  Hash formats are not expanded.
- The builder never opens the file. Reading and parsing happen when the command
  runs, and the file size is not bounded by the builder.
- For stdin, pass bytes in the execution options of `tmux_server:command/3` or
  `tmux_operation:start/3`. The transport bounds stdin and rendered arguments
  together to 256 KiB.
- `parse_only` requests native `-n`: parse without executing. `quiet` requests
  native missing-file suppression. Syntax and execution errors stay errors.
  Both default to false.

Configuration is trusted tmux code, with native directives and variable
expansion.

- Parse-only is not a sandbox.
- Execution can change state before it reports an error. Cancellation cannot
  roll that back.
- A successful source command does not mean background work it launched has
  finished. Check that work's own completion event.

## Coordinate channels

- `tmux_command:wait_for/2` takes a binary channel name and one action: `wait`,
  `signal`, `lock` or `unlock`. Submit the result through the same execution
  APIs.
- Channel names are server-wide. Use a name unique to the operation when other
  clients share the server.
- A signal wakes current waiters. On an unlocked channel with no waiters or
  pending wakeup, it keeps one wakeup for a later wait. Signalling again before
  a wait can clear that state.
- Send one signal per expected wait. Repeated signals are not counted or
  reliably coalesced. Use separate names for signalling and locking.
- `lock` and `unlock` are native advisory locks, not library-owned leases. A
  lock stays held after the acquiring client exits, until an explicit unlock.
- Cancelling a command does not undo a signal or release a lock it may have
  taken.
- After an uncertain lock outcome, coordinate in your application before you
  unlock. A blind unlock can release another client's lock.

# Build commands before running them

Prepare a session rename and a pane resize, then submit them explicitly.
Building validates the captured target and arguments without contacting tmux.
Execution checks the endpoint origin and returns the native one-shot result.

The program checks the name before execution, awaits the resize through an
operation handle, reads fresh dimensions and verifies that earlier rows keep
their values. The runner supplies the private server:

```console

```

```erlang
-module(command_demo).
-moduledoc "Build captured-target commands, then execute and inspect them.".
-export([run/2]).

-spec run(binary(), binary()) -> map().
run(Socket, Executable) ->
    Endpoint = #{socket_path => Socket, executable => Executable},
    {ok, Server} = tmux_server:open(Endpoint),
    tmux_scope:run_or_error(fun() ->
        {ok, Session} = tmux_session:create(Server,
            #{name => <<"commands">>, width => 120, height => 30,
              launch => #{argv => [<<"/bin/cat">>]}}),
        tmux_scope:run_or_error(fun() ->
            SessionId = tmux_model:get(id, Session),
            {ok, Snapshot} = tmux_server:snapshot(Server),
            [Anchor] = tmux_snapshot:panes(Snapshot),
            {ok, Pane} = tmux_pane:split(Anchor,
                #{direction => horizontal, size => {cells, 40},
                  launch => #{argv => [<<"/bin/cat">>]}}),
            {ok, Rename} = tmux_session:rename_command(
                Session, <<"commands-ready">>),
            {ok, Resize} = tmux_pane:resize_command(Pane, #{width => 60}),
            {ok, OtherEndpoint} = tmux_server:open(Endpoint),
            tmux_scope:run_or_error(fun() ->
                {error, #{code := different_owner, submitted := false}} =
                    tmux_server:command(OtherEndpoint, Rename, #{})
            end, fun() ->
                ok = tmux_server:close(OtherEndpoint)
            end),
            {ok, Before} = tmux_session:get(Server, SessionId),
            <<"commands">> = tmux_model:get(name, Before),
            40 = tmux_model:get(width, Pane),
            {ok, #{exit_status := 0, cleanup := complete}} =
                tmux_server:command(Server, Rename, #{}),
            {ok, Operation} = tmux_operation:start(Server, Resize, #{}),
            {ok, #{exit_status := 0, cleanup := complete}} =
                tmux_operation:await(Operation, 900),
            {ok, Current} = tmux_pane:get(Server, tmux_model:get(id, Pane)),
            60 = tmux_model:get(width, Current),
            {ok, Renamed} = tmux_session:get(Server, SessionId),
            <<"commands-ready">> = tmux_model:get(name, Renamed),
            <<"commands">> = tmux_model:get(name, Session),
            40 = tmux_model:get(width, Pane),
            #{name => <<"commands-ready">>, initial_width => 40,
              actual_width => 60, captured_values_unchanged => true,
              foreign_origin_rejected => true}
        end, fun() ->
            {ok, _} = tmux_session:kill(Session),
            ok
        end)
    end, fun() ->
        ok = tmux_server:close(Server)
    end).
```

## Keep the endpoint

- A command keeps its row's endpoint token. Submitting it through another
  endpoint returns `different_owner` with `submitted = false`, even when both
  endpoints use the same pane or session ID. The program checks this with a
  second handle to the same daemon.
- To act through another endpoint, bind the row there and build a new command.
  Bind a detached row with `tmux_server:bind/2` first.
- Building does not check that the endpoint is alive.

## Render without running

- `tmux_command:to_config/1` renders command syntax without executing it.
- Rendered configuration carries no origin token. Choose and validate the
  destination yourself.

# Support and remaining gaps

- **tmux:** 3.3a is the floor. Tested: 3.3a through 3.8, including
  intermediate releases, on Linux x86_64 and arm64.
- **Erlang/OTP:** 29 only. The application refuses to start on another release,
  and older-OTP branches are not maintained.
- **Native records:** experimental in OTP 29. Do not persist their internals or
  assume they carry over to another OTP line.
- **Built-in options and hooks:** each tmux release needs a catalogue entry. An
  unlisted release returns `unsupported_option_catalogue` for them.

| Platform | tmux releases in the required matrix |
| --- | --- |
| Ubuntu 24.04 x86_64 | 3.3a, 3.8 |
| Ubuntu 24.04 arm64 | 3.3a, 3.8 |

- CI uses only the latest stable Erlang/OTP and tests the oldest and newest
  tmux. Releases between them stay supported.
- Earlier intermediate-version results keep their recorded scope.
- Read the [workflow](../.github/workflows/ci.yml) jobs at the commit you will
  use. A minimum-version check does not prove support on every newer release.
- Tracking builds, macOS, native Windows and psmux are not advertised as
  supported.

## Linux process interface

- Linux must provide a readable `/proc/self/task/<pid>/children`, enabled by
  CONFIG_PROC_CHILDREN. The helper checks it before it launches a child.
- When it is missing, the call returns `unsupported_capability` with
  `capability => proc_children`, the OS `errno` and `outcome => not_started`.
- The [helper protocol](../apps/libtmux_erlang/c_src/README.md) covers cleanup
  evidence and the limits of native process ownership.

## Retained rows and upgrades

Native model version 2 adds a private captured-target association to each
observed row.

- Actions check the entity, stable ID, origin and snapshot ID. A pane
  association also keeps the observed window and index. A window-link
  association keeps its session, index and expected physical window.
- Actions reject edited target fields before dispatch. A well-formed mismatch
  returns `observation_mismatch`. Detached and malformed rows keep their
  validation errors.
- `tmux_server:bind/2` reads the requested target and returns a new actionable
  row. Ordinary record matching and detached constructors still work.
- The association holds identifiers, not the snapshot graph. It stops
  accidental retargeting through public row updates. It is not an authorization
  boundary against trusted code in the VM. The internal construction functions
  are implementation details.

Moving from model version 1:

- Discard version-1 rows and snapshots. Stop consumers that retain them, clear
  their process and ETS state, and observe the server afresh after a restart.
- There is no `appup` or `relup` conversion. Old or unknown model versions fail
  row validation. Validate a retained value before you read a field another
  model version added.
- Any exported-field addition, rename, removal or default change needs a model
  compatibility review, whatever the OTP version. Its changelog says whether
  retained values stay usable, need an explicit validated conversion, or must
  be discarded.
- Hot loading does not change fields in existing native values.

Storing rows:

- `tmux_model:to_map/1` extracts the documented fields from a valid row.
  Validate them with the destination model's constructor when you migrate data.
- The map loses actionable provenance. Bind it through a freshly constructed
  row before you act on it.
- It is not a versioned storage or cross-port wire format. Absence atoms,
  binary bytes and field inventories need an application-defined schema.

# Save a job's output and verify the consumer received it

This program opens a pane pipe before releasing the producer. A shell consumer
logs the expected bytes and signals after the write succeeds. The caller checks
the file before stopping the pipe. It never infers delivery from the command.

Compile the project:

```console
$ mise exec -- rebar3 compile
```

Run it on an owned server:

```console
$ mise exec -- escript tools/run_examples.escript pipe
```

<!-- example: examples/pipe_demo.erl -->

```erlang
-module(pipe_demo).
-moduledoc "Save terminal bytes after a consumer acknowledgement.".
-export([run/2]).

-spec run(binary(), binary()) -> map().
run(Socket, Executable) ->
    Suffix = binary:encode_hex(crypto:strong_rand_bytes(8), lowercase),
    Directory = <<"/tmp/ltm-pipe-example-", Suffix/binary>>,
    ok = file:make_dir(Directory),
    tmux_scope:run_or_error(fun() ->
        ok = file:change_mode(Directory, 8#700),
        Log = <<Directory/binary, "/job.log">>,
        {ok, Server} = tmux_server:open(
            #{socket_path => Socket, executable => Executable}),
        tmux_scope:run_or_error(fun() ->
            Native = <<(quote(Executable))/binary,
                " -N -S ", (quote(Socket))/binary, " wait-for ">>,
            Start = <<"start-", Suffix/binary>>,
            Done = <<"consumed-", Suffix/binary>>,
            Producer = <<"stty -onlcr && ", Native/binary, Start/binary,
                " && printf 'build complete\\n' && exec /bin/cat">>,
            {ok, Session} = tmux_session:create(Server,
                #{name => <<"pipe-example">>, launch => #{argv =>
                    [<<"/bin/sh">>, <<"-c">>, Producer]}}),
            tmux_scope:run_or_error(fun() ->
                {ok, Snapshot} = tmux_server:snapshot(Server),
                [Pane] = tmux_snapshot:panes(Snapshot),
                Payload = <<"build complete\n">>,
                Size = integer_to_binary(byte_size(Payload)),
                Consumer = <<"/usr/bin/head -c ", Size/binary,
                    " > ", (quote(Log))/binary, " && ", Native/binary,
                    "-S ", Done/binary, " && exec /bin/cat >/dev/null">>,
                {ok, Wait} = tmux_command:wait_for(Done, wait),
                {ok, Operation} = tmux_operation:start(Server, Wait, #{}),
                {ok, _} = tmux_pane:pipe(Pane, #{shell => Consumer}, #{}),
                {ok, Signal} = tmux_command:wait_for(Start, signal),
                {ok, _} = tmux_server:command(Server, Signal, #{}),
                {ok, #{cleanup := complete}} =
                    tmux_operation:await(Operation, 900),
                {ok, Payload} = file:read_file(Log),
                {ok, _} = tmux_pane:stop_pipe(Pane),
                #{log => Payload, bytes_written => byte_size(Payload),
                  consumer_acknowledged => true}
            end, fun() ->
                {ok, _} = tmux_session:kill(Session),
                ok
            end)
        end, fun() ->
            ok = tmux_server:close(Server)
        end)
    end, fun() ->
        ok = file:del_dir_r(Directory)
    end).

quote(Value) ->
    Escaped = binary:replace(Value, <<"'">>, <<"'\\''">>, [global]),
    <<"'", Escaped/binary, "'">>.
```

- The program uses the Linux utilities `stty`, `/usr/bin/head` and `/bin/cat`.

## Choose direction and replacement

- `tmux_pane:pipe/3` takes an explicit shell-command map and a registered
  physical pane. It escapes hash and strftime directives before tmux expands
  the text.
- The shell still interprets the command. The program's `quote/1` handles
  values it inserts into shell code. This operation takes shell code, not
  executable argv.
- `tmux_command:literal_format/2` documents the encoding limits. A command with
  percent signs above tmux's 8191-byte time-format limit returns
  `format_limit` before dispatch, so an existing pipe survives a replacement
  that cannot be represented.

| Direction | Connection |
| --- | --- |
| `output` (default) | Pane PTY output to child stdin |
| `input` | Child stdout to pane input |
| `both` | Both connections |

- Terminal modes affect these bytes.
- This is not rendered screen capture and not a replay of earlier history. It
  is not an Erlang subscription with library flow control.
- Child stderr is discarded. Unused directions go to the null device.
- The API does not copy the pane's working directory or environment into the
  child.
- Starting a pipe normally replaces an existing one. `toggle => true` maps to
  native `-o`: an open pipe closes without starting another, and a closed pipe
  opens. It does not keep an open pipe.

## Tell the pipe from its process

- A successful action proves command completion. It does not prove the shell
  ran, the consumer was ready, bytes arrived or the process exited. The program
  watches the consumer's own file write.
- `tmux_pane:stop_pipe/1` closes the native connection and can discard pending
  bytes. Wait for the consumer's acknowledgement first when delivery matters.
- Closing does not kill or wait for a shell process. A consumer that does not
  finish at EOF needs application-level coordination.
- `tmux_server:close/1` leaves the borrowed pane and its tmux-owned pipe alone.

See [jobs and operations](jobs.md) for library-owned command clients and
[configuration and signals](configuration.md) for native wait channels.

# Native commands and capability floors

Generated from pinned tmux source profiles. These are native
parser declarations, not an inventory of implemented Erlang facades,
complete argument validation or runtime qualification. Canonical names

available through `tmux_command:raw/2`.

supported architectures. See
[compatibility](compatibility.md) for platform and API qualification.

# Build and browse the native API

Contracts live in Erlang `-moduledoc`, `-doc` and specs. ExDoc renders them
from the compiler's EEP-48 chunks as searchable module, function and type
pages.

- Source links open captured files with line anchors and content digests.
- An unchanged file also links to its exact Git commit. A changed file is
  labelled a working-tree preview.

Compile the project:

```console
$ mise exec -- rebar3 compile
```

Prepare the checksum-pinned ExDoc tool. This step uses the network:

```console
$ mise exec -- escript scripts/docs/build_docs.erl --prepare
```

Build the browser without fetching dependencies:

```console
$ mise exec -- escript scripts/docs/build_docs.erl
```

Open `_build/docs/core/index.html`.

- This is a local build, not a published HexDocs page.
- The build refreshes compiled modules first, and warnings fail it.
- It uses the OTP 29 build of ExDoc. It reads compiler chunks directly because
  the older EDoc source path rejects native-record attributes.

- [Contributor checks](../.github/CONTRIBUTING.md) run the native shell

## Types at application boundaries

- Entity constructors take generated maps such as `t:tmux_model:pane_input/0`.
  Dialyzer sees the required fields and scalar categories.
- Optional observations keep `not_loaded` and `unavailable`. Nullable fields
  also accept `none`.
- Numeric fields accept integral floats, which normalize to integers.
- Runtime validation checks bounds, ID syntax, UTF-8 and derived values. Use
  `tmux_model:new/2` for dynamic maps and handle its
  `t:tmux_schema:error_detail/0` result.
- `t:tmux_select:t/1` describes the intended row type. Dialyzer in OTP 29 does
  not always substitute actual argument types into generic return variables. A
  selection passed through `tmux_select:one/1` can lose its entity type.
- A clean analysis does not prove every pane and window relationship. Keep
  native patterns and runtime action validation at those boundaries.
- The
  [OTP contract solver](https://github.com/erlang/otp/blob/OTP-29.1.2/lib/dialyzer/src/dialyzer_contracts.erl#L477-L502)
  records this generic constraint limitation.

# Project policy

This port provides the `libtmux_erlang` core application.

The [architecture decision record](adr-0001-architecture.md) explains the
selected design, alternatives, consequences and conditions for reconsideration.

## OTP application boundaries

Develop the application in the Rebar3 umbrella layout. It is an independent
package boundary with its own metadata, license and changelog.

| Application | Responsibility | Library dependencies |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `libtmux_erlang` | tmux transport, operations, domain objects, snapshots and queries | OTP applications |

Consumers use public APIs through installed packages; source paths and private
core modules are not integration boundaries. Additional packages need their own
reusable responsibility and explicit consumer dependencies.

Package qualification must install the core outside the umbrella. A successful
umbrella build alone does not prove that an independently installed package
works; see [current support](compatibility.md).

## Runtime dependencies

Use the latest stable Erlang/OTP baseline and native OTP facilities. Use OTP
JSON for documents. Prefer module functions, native records, specs, tagged
results and supervised processes where ownership requires them.

Keep Erlang runtime dependencies within OTP. An exception requires a concrete
capability need, maintenance assessment and recorded architecture decision.
Test, build and documentation tools are separate from runtime dependencies.

Support covers tmux 3.3a–3.8, including intermediate releases, on Linux x86_64
and arm64. CI uses only the latest stable Erlang/OTP release and samples the
oldest supported and newest stable tmux releases. Verify upstream releases
before updating the exact pins. Historical results retain their recorded scope.

The Linux transport uses the bundled C11 executable for bounded I/O and owned
process retirement. It is built from packaged source with recorded provenance.

The layout follows [Rebar3 application organization](https://rebar3.org/docs/basic_usage/)
and [OTP application boundaries and dependencies](https://www.erlang.org/doc/system/applications.html).
